evidence: Compiled G2 as G1 plus exactly six patches, one per measured G1 failure, applied by build_g2.py from G1 sha256 c76b73b1ca3ff44f9256f08bb2d35af90c906a646e70cff97d5a546af301f47a to G2 sha256 3d963e28be419ceb16d6556efb73c5e1eac72d633fe6196d107a19171af4d021 (+5938 bytes). The builder reads the failure list out of unit 062's committed g1-measurement.json and refuses any change whose case_id is not a measured failure, and refuses any anchor that does not match exactly once, so the lineage in g2/lineage.json describes the actual diff. Lineage, all disposition SUPERSEDE: G2-CHANGE-001 complete_unit+ingest_result for H01, G2-CHANGE-002 allocate_fence for H02, G2-CHANGE-003 ingest_result for H03, G2-CHANGE-004 scan_recovery for H04, G2-CHANGE-005 hash_chain_event+verify_chain for H05, G2-CHANGE-006 read_object_bytes for H06. Measured G2 on the identical frozen suite bytes as G0 and G1 (public 345b266db4c9ea415d83de1505f06ded8f7c276d5ca88935bfc60aa8f23eb152, holdout c15cfe57b318a8cf7aba12fd5c6e715d03fab5fee3be381771562daa18fe91d5, seal 782b235bbea3168ce77d2d876040cb40b1a903ac61c32cb32047ca15c150c5da): public 16/16 pass_rate 1.0, holdout 10/10 pass_rate 1.0, combined 26/26 pass_rate 1.0, false_green_rate 0.0. All six G1 failures are repaired with real refusals, for example H02 went from 48 allocations returning 40 duplicate tokens with the counter left at 8 to 48 concurrent allocations producing 48 distinct tokens and a final counter of 48, and H05 now reports 'chain truncated; the recorded head is sequence 3 but 2 events remain'. Zero regressions on the frozen suites: every case G1 passed, G2 still passes. Independently checked for regression against the repository's own 58 baseline tests, which this cohort did not author: they load the factory by relative path, so a sandbox with each generation in tools/ runs them unmodified. 58 ran / 58 ok under G1 and 58 ran / 58 ok under G2, parse completeness confirmed against unittest's own printed count, 0 regressed and 0 disappeared tests. That check mattered: the obvious H01 repair, requiring the completed document to be byte-identical to the ingested one, would have broken every legitimate completion because the coordinator must stamp parent_ingested_at before the COMPLETED contract validates, so the binding is over result identity with the coordinator-stamped fields normalised. successor_claim.py evaluated the preregistered decision rule and returned SUPPORTED with successor_lift 0.2308 against the preregistered minimum of 0.05; its tests prove it returns REFUSED for sub-threshold lift, for a regression, for an UNSUPPORTED case replacing a PASS, for a worse false_green_rate, for a failure in the independent suite, and for runs measured on different suite bytes. 26 tests pass under python3 -I -m unittest discover.
falsifiable_hypothesis: A successor compiled from G1 failures and accepted lessons outperforms G1 on preregistered metrics with no quality regression.
limitations: The producer who authored the public suite also authored G2, so suite independence rests on commit chronology and sha256 freezing plus the sealed holdout from unit 059 and the repository's independently authored 58-test baseline, not on a separate author. G2 scores 26/26, which means the frozen suite can no longer discriminate further improvement and any future successor will show zero lift on it; a ceiling reached is not the same as a system proven correct. false_green_rate(G2) is 0.0 by the empty-denominator convention rather than by observation: G2 has zero cases that report success while broken, so reported_success_count is 0 and there is no denominator. Per the preregistration's anti-tuning commitment the metric definition is retained unchanged and this defect is recorded rather than fixed. Two known asserted fields were deliberately left unrepaired because no measured failure covers them: duplicate_callback_count is still the literal 0 in scan_recovery, and assert_fence_current still compares only fence values without holder identity. The fence lock is an O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock file, which is atomic on a local filesystem but not guaranteed on NFS, and a process killed between creating and unlinking the lock blocks allocation until the 30s timeout rather than recovering. G2 is measured, not deployed: the live workstreams/po03/tools/transactional_factory.py is untouched, and the package is staged in this unit's subtree for the controller to ingest into successor/g2/.
